providers.summary: GPU cloud selling on-demand instances by the minute, with no spot market and no contract. The page says nothing about VAT.

providers.name: Baseten

providers.summary: AMD only. Each rate is one GPU-hour on the card page's own pricing block; the page names no machine type, no location and no reserved term, so none is shown here. Capacity is ordered through their form, not a self-serve console.

The page shows the commitment rates rounded to the cent.

providers.name: Canopy Wave

providers.summary: Rents whole bare-metal servers by the hour, eight GPUs each, priced per server; shown here per GPU. The monthly prices beside them assume a year paid in advance and are not listed. Its servers are "fail in place": a failed server is replaced, its storage is not.

providers.name: centron
providers.notes: Static GPU table (GPU, VRAM, € per hour*, € per month), columns by header; VRAM cell must equal the mapped card's memory; gpu_only (VM resources vCPU/RAM/SSD priced in a second table); hourly figure as printed, rounded per the page's footnote (month = 720 unrounded hours); EUR net of VAT ("All prices are subject to statutory VAT", businesses only); on_demand, per_gpu, region null (one data centre, Hallstadt)
providers.summary: German cloud provider with its own data centre in Hallstadt. Its GPU price list gives an hourly and a monthly price per dedicated GPU in euro, excluding VAT, and sells to businesses only. The figure here is the GPU alone: the processor, memory and storage of the instance are priced separately on the same page and added on top. The hourly figures are rounded, as the page notes.

providers.notes: serverless GPU per second x 3600, GPU only; bare H100 unmapped
providers.summary: Serverless: GPUs are billed by the second while code runs, shown here as a GPU-hour, with memory and storage billed separately.

providers.notes: One table per GPU; the 1 x size read (larger sizes are exact multiples); on-demand plus 12- and 36-month commitments, the 6- and 24-month terms not recorded. H100 table headed H100 SXM.

providers.name: Clore.ai
providers.notes: marketplace, keyless feed; trimmed floor of the 5 cheapest verified single-GPU on-demand listings, withheld when the window cannot carry a floor (fewer than 3 listings, or a median over 3x the cheapest ask); the feed prices per day and the renter fee is read from /marketplace/renter_fees each run, so the figure is price * 1.05 / 24; spot bids and multi-GPU machines not read
providers.summary: A marketplace where hosts set their own prices. Each figure is a floor - the median of the five cheapest listings that Clore itself marks verified ("rating above 4 with reviews"), rentable and payable in dollars - withheld when too few are listed. Clore lists a price per day; the figure here is that price with the renter fee Clore charges, divided by 24, which is what its own table shows per hour. Machines with several GPUs and its spot market are not read.

providers.name: Cloud.ru Evolution
providers.notes: RUB listing, VAT included as printed: the tariff annex prints each hourly rate with VAT, without VAT and the 22% VAT apart, and the with-VAT column is published (owner's decision 2026-09-28). Scope instance - whole GPU virtual machines with their own vCPU and RAM, шт./час. One quote per card, the lowest price per GPU, per node with the count read from the row's name (also the instance label). Region null: the annex names none. Names: "H100 94 GB PCI без NVLink" is h100-nvl, "H100 PCI без NVLink" h100-pcie (the 94 GB card is priced apart and dearer), "H100 NVLink" the neutral h100, "A100 40Гб PCI" a100-40; the memoryless "A100 PCI без NVLink" (11 rows, the cheapest A100s) is reported unmapped, not guessed
providers.summary: The largest Russian public cloud, formerly SberCloud. Its GPU rates are published not on a marketing page but in the tariff annex of the contract (version 260909, in force 9 September 2026), which prices whole virtual machines by the hour in roubles. The page prints each rate with and without Russian VAT; the figure here is the one with VAT, what a buyer pays. Each card shows the machine with the lowest price per GPU, often a multi-GPU one. The dollar figure uses the Bank of Russia's official rate of the day.

providers.summary: Rents single GPUs by the minute from a prepaid balance, in public beta with no SLA. The machines belong to suppliers who list idle servers with it, but the hourly price is the platform's own, one per card, so each figure is read as a list price, not as a market floor.

providers.name: CloudPe
providers.notes: INR listing, GPU tab of the pricing page only. Hourly column read; Monthly and Annual (12 %) are month-prices with no term named, so no reserved rate is made of them. Cheapest single-card configuration per card (L4 has three host sizes); x2 and x4 nodes are reported unmapped, not published. Scope instance: each row names vCPU, RAM and NVMe. "NVIDIA RTX Pro 6000" prints no memory or edition and maps to rtx-pro-6000. No GST or tax mentioned on the page. The server sends no charset; the body is decoded as the UTF-8 the page declares.
providers.summary: An Indian cloud with data centres in India. The pricing page lists GPU virtual machines by the hour in rupees, each row a fixed machine (vCPU, memory and disk named), and the rate here is the cheapest single-GPU machine for each card. The page says nothing about GST or other tax. The dollar figure uses the ECB reference rate of the day.

Prices are listed in rupees per hour for whole GPU instances, with a discount for a 1, 6 or 12-month commitment; the figure here is the on-demand one, as printed - the page states no GST. Each card shows the instance with the lowest price per GPU, often an eight-card one. The dollar figure uses the European Central Bank's reference rate of the day. The page also offers its own dollar figures; those are never read, because it says itself that its conversion failed.

providers.summary: Four series priced separately on one page, and each is listed here under its own name: Nova single-GPU VMs with NVLink, the Atlas and Yotta pods, and the Orion nodes, whose eight-GPU bare-metal machines are the cheapest way this provider sells an H200 or an RTX PRO 6000. vCPU and memory are included in every rate; storage is billed on top. Nova's spot rate is for capacity that may be reclaimed when demand rises. The page draws three of its four price tables from files it loads itself, and prints "Getting Real Time Cost..." while one of them is unavailable.

providers.summary: Daytona sells sandboxes billed by the hour. The GPU rate here is the GPU alone; the sandbox's vCPUs, memory and storage are billed on top at the rates on the same page. Preemptible capacity can be reclaimed.

The page says nothing about VAT.

Each figure is a floor - the median of the five cheapest asks on machines whose Stability and 30-Day Machine Uptime, as Octa.space prints them, are both 95% or more and which have at least one successful rental - withheld when too few qualify. Octa.space prints no verified badge; the thresholds are ours. The price is the machine's Total Cost as its card shows it, including the default 100 GB disk; traffic is billed per GB on top. Machines rented whole are a separate row; machines mixing two GPU models are not read.

High priority is never preempted by other workloads and is shown here as on-demand; Medium, Low and Lowest may be preempted, and are shown as spot. The price covers the GPU with the vCPU and memory the page says are included. Not shown: CPU-only groups, and reserved and volume deals, which publish no rate.

fees.value: The bare-metal GPU plan bundles CPU, RAM, local NVMe and a bandwidth allowance in one hourly_cost. www.vultr.com/pricing returned 403.
Plan allowance (15,360 GB on the GPU bare-metal plans), then $0.01/GB. Inbound is not metered.
A stopped instance keeps billing in full (CPU, RAM, storage, IP) until it is destroyed.
Hourly, minimum one hour. Monthly cap of 730 h for Cloud GPU and 672 h for bare metal (our rows are bare metal).

providers.notes: bare-metal plans endpoint /v2/plans-metal (keyless); a rate is published only where the endpoint says the plan can be deployed that way (deploy_ondemand, deploy_preemptible), so eight plans that state an hourly_cost while saying deploy_ondemand:false are not published as on-demand rates; preemptible recorded as spot, and skipped when equal to the plan's own on-demand price (the same figure twice); the fractional cloud GPU plans in /v2/plans are not read
providers.summary: Read from Vultr's own open plans endpoint, api.vultr.com/v2/plans-metal, which anyone can open without a key and which each row links beside the provider name; the name leads to Vultr's pricing page, which answers our reader 403 but opens in a browser. Each plan there is priced twice, on demand and preemptible, and says of each price whether it can be deployed that way; only a price it says you can deploy is shown here. Prices are for the whole machine, divided by its number of GPUs. Plans that sell a fraction of a GPU are not listed.

providers.name: Yandex Cloud
providers.notes: Rendered price list (providers/_render.py) of the one service Compute Cloud - GPU; rows with unit "GPU × час" only, gpu_only scope (vCPU and RAM are separate lines); RUB with VAT as printed ("Все цены в рублях и тенге указаны с НДС"); обычной ВМ = on_demand, прерываемой ВМ = spot; a row not in force today by its Действует с/до dates is skipped; V100 32 GB, A100 80 GB, T4 16 GB per /ru/docs/compute/concepts/gpus; Gen2 (80 GB), GPU PLATFORM V4 (141 GB) and T4i name no NVIDIA card and are unmapped; instance = product name; region null
providers.summary: Russian public cloud (Yandex). Its price list bills a GPU virtual machine as separate lines - the GPU, each vCPU and each gigabyte of memory - so the figure here is the GPU line alone, and the processor and memory a machine needs are added on top. Prices are in roubles and include VAT, as the list states; preemptible machines, which Yandex may stop at any time, are shown as spot. The dollar figure uses the Bank of Russia's official rate of the day.

providers.name: Yotta Labs
providers.notes: GPU pods at one list price per card (On-demand, Spot columns); read as a rate card, per GPU; a spot cell at or above its own on-demand rate is not read; bare H100 -> h100
providers.summary: Rents GPU pods by the second through its own orchestration across data centres, at one hourly list price per card. The Spot column is read where it prints a rate below the same row's on-demand rate; a spot figure above it is left out. Not the Indian Yotta Data Services.

providers.name: YTL AI Cloud
providers.notes: Static "On Demand GPU" box (GPU Model, Memory/Bandwidth, Price (per hour)) of Bootstrap div rows; memory cell must start with the mapped card's 192GB; gpu_only (object storage is its own box); MYR via the ECB cross rate; the page says nothing about tax; on_demand, per_gpu, region null (hosted in Malaysia); committed-use discounts via partners print no figure
providers.summary: Malaysian GPU cloud of YTL Power, hosted on sovereign infrastructure in Malaysia. Its price page lists one on-demand GPU, the NVIDIA GB200, by the hour in Malaysian ringgit; object storage is priced separately and is not included here. Discounts for committed use are sold through partners and carry no published figure. The dollar figure uses the ECB reference rate of the day.
